items.title: Nepal: IRDR Rapid Analysis Report - Scientific Anatomy of the 26 August 2026 Bhotekoshi Flash Flood
items.summary: Country: Nepal Source: Integrated Research on Disaster Risk Please refer to the attached file. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY The 26 August 2026 Bhotekoshi flash flood appears to have been triggered by an ice, rock and soil mass failure around the Deding/Langtang region rather than intense localized rainfall. The failure likely blocked the river and formed a temporary natural dam for about 18-19 hours. The dam then breached around 8:30-8:37 a.m. on 26 August, releasing a large volume of water, ice, rock, sediment and debris. Continued inflow from the Mala River and other tributaries may have masked the upstream blockage. The steep gradient and narrow…

items.title: Nepal Floods: School children reunited with families after being stranded – Save the Children
items.summary: Country: Nepal Source: Save the Children KATHMANDU, 28 August 2026 – Nine school children have been reunited with their families after being stranded at school for two days by the devastating flash floods in Northern Nepal, as rescue efforts continue to reach other students, Save the Children said. The children arrived at an aid distribution point where Save the Children is working after walking from their school. Many children in the area travel long distances to their schools and were cut off in the aftermath of the massive surge of floodwater. With support from Save the Children, they were able to find their families. At least 69 schools…

items.title: WVI Nepal Declares Category I National Response to Flash Floods in Rasuwa and Nuwakot
items.summary: Country: Nepal Source: World Vision A major flash flood entered Nepal through the Bhote Koshi River at around 9:00 AM on 26 August, causing significant damage in Rasuwa and Nuwakot districts. The worst-affected areas include Timure, Rasuwagadhi, and Syabrubesi, where homes, markets, roads, and hydropower infrastructure were destroyed. Rescue and relief operations are underway, and authorities have issued alerts for communities along the Trishuli River. World Vision Nepal is closely monitoring the evolving situation and coordinating with government authorities, local partners, and humanitarian actors to assess the needs of affected…

items.title: Rescuers grapple with mountain of challenges after the Nepal-Tibet floods
items.summary: Emergency services are rushing to find survivors and treat the wounded after a devastating flash flood on the border of Nepal and Tibet on Wednesday killed more than 500 people, with over a thousand still missing. But the remote and rugged terrain, as well as the risk of further flooding from upstream lakes formed by piles of debris, make their work as delicate as it is dangerous.

items.title: Chinese control of information hampers assessment of Tibet flood damage
items.summary: Scale of devastation emerges in Nepal as reporters reach disaster area, but Chinese state media focus more on rescue efforts Nepal-Tibet flash flood – latest updates In the days since an enormous glacier in the Himalayas snapped away from a mountaintop and cascaded into the valley below, the true scale of the devastation caused by the flash floods in Nepal and Tibet is still unfolding. But the picture is emerging far more quickly in Nepal than in China, where strict controls on the flow of information from one of its most sensitive regions are hampering the public’s understanding of events. items.title: Nepal floods explained: The chain of events behind the disaster
items.summary: A glacier broke apart. An ice and rock avalanche followed. Then came an earthquake, before a landslide triggered devastating floods that tore through kilometres of valley. This is what happened along the Nepal-China border, where rescue teams are still trying to recover survivors 48 hours after the catastrophe. FRANCE 24 breaks down the chain of events and the scientific explanations behind the disaster.

items.title: List Of Indians, Locals, Tourists Missing In Flood-Hit Nepal
items.summary: More than 1,400 people remain missing, according to news agency AFP, citing authorities. So far, 644 have been identified, which includes 178 Indians.

items.title: Nepal flood survivors rescued from hydropower tunnel
items.summary: Nepali soldiers rescued around 100 people trapped inside a flooded hydropower tunnel as the death toll from the Nepal-China floods continued to climb, with more than 1,500 people still missing. Rescue efforts were briefly suspended over fears that an overflowing landslide lake could trigger more flooding, while families across the disaster zone continue searching for loved ones.

items.title: Nepal: A newly formed lake is sparking fears of more flooding along the Chinese border
items.summary: Rescue operations are continuing after the devastating Nepal-China floods, but authorities have ordered emergency teams to stay on high alert as a newly formed upstream lake threatens to burst and trigger fresh flooding. Satellite imagery suggests the lake formed in the same area where a glacier collapse on Wednesday unleashed the deadly chain of events. FRANCE 24's Navodita Kumari has the latest from India.
